temperature, different time: thickness decides how long the heat takes to reach the middle. Size Air fryer Oven Thin, about ⅓ inch (8 mm) 375°F / 190°C · 8 min 400°F / 205°C · 10 min Standard, about ½ inch (1.3 cm) 375°F / 190°C · 10 min 400°F / 205°C · 13 min Thick, about ¾ inch (2 cm) 375°F / 190°C · 14 min 400°F / 205°C · 18 min Domed, shrunken and smoky Ground beef behaves nothing like a steak. As a patty heats, its proteins contract and pull the edges inwards, so the middle bulges into a dome that cooks unevenly and will not sit flat in a bun. Meanwhile the fat melts out and drips onto the hot drawer, where it can smoke. Pressing a shallow dimple into the centre of each raw patty keeps it flat as it shrinks; a drawer that is cleaned between batches, with a splash of water under the basket on some models, keeps the smoke down. The other mistake is borrowing steak doneness. Mincing spreads surface bacteria all through the meat, so a burger has to reach 160°F in the middle, not the medium-rare figure that is fine for a whole steak. Worked example Four ½-inch patties of 80/20 beef, about 5 oz each, with a dimple pressed into each and salted just before cooking. Preheat for 4 minutes, cook at 375°F for 10 minutes, flipping at 5. Thin smash-style patties take about 8 minutes and thick ¾-inch ones about 14. Add cheese for the final minute. Under a conventional oven setting the same patties need 400°F for about 13 minutes. How to tell they are done Insert the thermometer from the side into the middle of the patty: 160°F (71°C) is the food-safety target for ground beef, and at that point the juices run clear and the centre is brown with no red. Colour alone can mislead, because some beef browns early and some stays pink when fully cooked. A burger that bulged in the middle will be done at the edges before the centre, so measure in the thickest point. Before they go in Choose beef with around 20% fat; leaner mince turns dry. Handle it lightly and shape patties slightly wider than the bun, since they shrink. Make the dimple with your thumb, about half the depth of the patty. Salt only the outside, right before cooking, or the meat turns sausage-like. No oil needed. About 10 minutes at 375°F for ½-inch fresh patties, flipped at 5 minutes. Thin patties take around 8 minutes and thick ¾-inch ones around 14. What temperature should a burger be cooked to? 160°F (71°C) in the centre. That is higher than steak because grinding mixes surface bacteria into the meat. Can I cook frozen burger patties in the air fryer? Yes, at the same temperature. Add about 4–6 minutes to the fresh time, flip halfway, and still check for 160°F in the middle. Separate patties that froze together first. Why do my burgers puff up in the air fryer? The edges shrink faster than the middle, which pushes the centre up. A thumb dimple in each raw patty keeps them flat. What is the oven equivalent for burgers? 400°F for around 13 minutes on a rack in a conventional oven, flipped once.
